CAR-T QSP — R ↔︎ Julia Full-Trajectory Cross-Validation

6-state LD-recovery model · rxode2 (lsoda) vs DifferentialEquations.jl (Rodas5P)

Published

June 7, 2026

Overview

This report cross-validates the canonical 6-state CAR-T QSP model (LD-recovery structure; see canonical_spec.md) implemented independently in rxode2 and DifferentialEquations.jl. Both stacks integrate identical equations on the same grid (0–365 d, step 0.5) with matched scalar tolerances (rtol = atol = 1e-8). A neutral scipy solve is included as an optional third anchor. Agreement is a transcription-equivalence check — it confirms the model is encoded identically in both ecosystems, not that the model is biologically correct.

Acceptance: per-state scaled relative error |a − b| / max(|a|, |b|, floor) ≤ 1e-4. The floor stops the high/mid clones — which cross zero near day 22 — from registering numerical-noise points as failures (the near-zero-state lesson from R validation layer 1).

Inputs (produced by the prior run steps, then quarto render this file):

  • r_traj.csv — Rscript cart_qsp_ld_rxode2.R
  • julia_traj.csv — julia cart_qsp_ld.jl
  • reference_traj.csv — python cart_qsp_ld_reference.py (optional)

Trajectory overlays

If the encodings agree, the thin Julia line sits inside the thick rxode2 line, and scipy (dotted) overlays both. Any visible separation flags a real divergence.

Scaled-error traces (rxode2 vs Julia)

Where, and how large, any disagreement is over time. Dashed red is the acceptance threshold.
